Subject: Post-demo follow-up: deployment mode & data residency

Hi Liam / Sofia,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciate you walking us through the EuroBank use cases. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Summary of requirements we captured:
  - Primary requirement: EU-only processing and storage for customer PII (regulatory constraint).
  - Secondary: APAC-based product teams need lower-latency access for non-PII workflows.
  - Some internal teams may require private networking / audit log retention longer than default.

- Deployment modes we discussed (and when we typically recommend them):
  - Hosted API (EU regions): fastest to go live, per-region processing and retention controls, multi-tenant but region-isolated for data in flight & at rest when requests are pinned to EU.
  - Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools in your cloud region or our dedicated tenancy — good when you need predictable throughput and stronger isolation without full VPC setup.
  - Private VPC / On-prem: full network isolation, customer-managed networking, and on-prem packaging for regulated workloads.

Action items / next steps:
1) Can you confirm which datasets are considered PII and must stay in EU? (high-level is fine)
2) Is cross-region routing for non-PII acceptable (i.e., EU for PII, APAC for non-PII)?
3) Would you like a technical deep-dive (Aditya) to go over region pinning, network topology, and audit log controls?

We can also share a short packet (SOC 2 summary, region availability, and an architecture diagram) — I'll loop Aditya in to provide the technical details.

Thanks,

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the recap — helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- PII scope: customer financial records + any KYC artifacts must remain in the EU. Operational logs that contain no customer identifiers could be processed in APAC if needed, but we'd prefer to keep as much as possible in-region.
- Latency: our APAC product team has strict latency SLAs for internal tools used by branch offices — they prefer APAC-hosted endpoints for those non-PII models.
- Isolation: is the Hosted EU option single-tenant or shared? For PII workloads we need assurance that data does not leave the EU and that tenancy isolation meets our compliance needs.

Can you send your SOC 2 summary and any documentation about regional isolation? Also attaching our security questionnaire — please have someone on your team fill the technical sections.

Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: deployment mode & data residency

Hi Liam / Sofia — thanks for the clear questions. Quick technical notes and options: 

1) Hosted API (EU regions)
   - We operate hosted endpoints in multiple EU regions (e.g., eu-west-1, eu-central-1). When requests are directed to an EU-hosted endpoint, processing and storage (for logs/kv caching tied to that request) remain in-region by default.
   - Hosted is multi-tenant by control plane but we provide strong logical separation and per-tenant encryption keys. For many customers this meets compliance when combined with our SOC 2 controls and contractual commitments.

2) Dedicated capacity
   - Reserved GPU pools that are logically isolated to your account. Runs in a chosen region and provides stronger tenancy isolation and dedicated throughput guarantees. Good middle ground if you want less ops overhead than VPC but stronger isolation than hosted.

3) Private VPC / On-prem
   - Full network isolation (customer VPC peering or on-prem package). All inference compute and key management can be placed inside your network boundary. This is the option we recommend for regulated PII workloads that cannot live on a shared tenancy.

4) Cross-region routing and hybrid approaches
   - We can implement routing policies so PII-bound requests always hit EU-hosted or Dedicated nodes, while non-PII traffic from APAC teams hits APAC nodes. This can be enforced at the API gateway layer and by request-scoped metadata.

Attachments I'm including:
- redwood-soc2-summary.pdf — overview of controls and evidence links
- redwood-region-availability.pdf — list of available regions and typical latency profiles
- deployment-architecture-diagram.png — example hybrid deployment (Hosted EU for PII + APAC Dedicated for non-PII)

Next recommended steps:
- If EuroBank can accept hosted multi-tenant in EU for a subset of workloads, we can pilot there quickly (1–2 weeks).
- For EU PII that requires isolation, we recommend Dedicated or Private VPC. We can provide an estimate for Dedicated capacity and a checklist for Private VPC onboarding.

Happy to walk through the security questionnaire — I'll have our compliance engineer fill the technical sections once you confirm which deployment model you're leaning toward.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
